Health Information

Most people infected with avian influenza have no or mild symptoms. Symptoms may include flu-like illness such as fever, cough, runny nose, weakness, headache, muscle aches, sore throat, gastrointestinal symptoms and shortness of breath as well as conjunctivitis (red, sore eyes). It can take up to 10 days for symptoms to develop after exposure.

Question.TranslatedText: Complete?

I am calling from [LPHU]. We are working with the Department of Health and the Department of Agriculture in Victoria. Privacy statement: [LPHU] is committed to protecting your privacy. [LPHU] is collecting this health information in response to an outbreak of avian influenza. To facilitate the outbreak investigation, we may share your health information with Department of Health or Agriculture Victoria. If you do not provide us with the information requested, we will not be able to investigate your possible exposure to avian influenza. You may access the information you provide to [LPHU]. As you may be aware, we have been notified of an avian influenza ("bird flu") virus outbreak among chickens at [FARM] . We are calling because you have been identified as potentially having been exposed to this virus. The chance of humans becoming infected with bird flu virus is low. However, people who come into contact with infected birds or contaminated bird products as part of their daily work or activities may be at risk of becoming infected. We are calling to get some more information from you and give you advice on what you need to do.

ItemDef.Name: symptoms
ItemDef.redcap:SectionHeader:
Health Information

Most people infected with avian influenza have no or mild symptoms. Symptoms may include flu-like illness such as fever, cough, runny nose, weakness, headache, muscle aches, sore throat, gastrointestinal symptoms and shortness of breath as well as conjunctivitis (red, sore eyes). It can take up to 10 days for symptoms to develop after exposure.

Question.TranslatedText: Key points for education: While bird flu spreads easily between birds, it does not commonly spread from birds to humans Because you have had contact with birds on a farm with a bird flu outbreak, you have a risk of becoming infected Most people infected with avian influenza have no or mild symptoms. Symptoms may include flu-like illness such as fever, cough, runny nose, weakness, headache, muscle aches, sore throat, gastrointestinal symptoms and shortness of breath as well as conjunctivitis (red, sore eyes). It can take up to 10 days for symptoms to develop after exposure. Please monitor for symptoms for 10 days after your last exposure to infected birds or contaminated bird products (while not wearing full PPE)
Question.redcap:FormattedTranslatedText:
Key points for education:

  • While bird flu spreads easily between birds, it does not commonly spread from birds to humans
  • Because you have had contact with birds on a farm with a bird flu outbreak, you have a risk of becoming infected
  • Most people infected with avian influenza have no or mild symptoms. Symptoms may include flu-like illness such as fever, cough, runny nose, weakness, headache, muscle aches, sore throat, gastrointestinal symptoms and shortness of breath as well as conjunctivitis (red, sore eyes). It can take up to 10 days for symptoms to develop after exposure.
  • Please monitor for symptoms for 10 days after your last exposure to infected birds or contaminated bird products (while not wearing full PPE)
